description: Produced-water radium-226 concentration (post-precipitation), conventional, world default
notes: Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): value is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. Centre 5 Bq/L world conventional: below the US conventional centre because US basin data are Appalachian/Gulf-weighted and Norway (3.5-4.1 Bq/L, S0307/S0308) and the RP 135 reference (10 Bq/L, S0204) bracket it. No Ra data exist in the NPWGD for TX, OK, KS or LA, so the US volume-weighted value rests on ANL state volumes (S0313) and basin means (Appalachian conventional 28.5, Gulf Coast 20.8, Powder River 0.52 Bq/L, S0303). Middle East, Russia and China have no measurements (gap). Applied to produced_water_m3 x (1 - unconventional share). Rest of world = XWL driver minus USA driver. Country-specific row (USA) overrides.

description: Produced-water radium-226 concentration, conventional, USA

description: Produced-water radium-226 concentration, unconventional (shale and tight), world default

description: Rn-222 released by associated-gas flaring per tonne of crude produced, world 1900-1993
notes: Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): value is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. description: Rn-222 in marketed gas delivered to end users (reaches burners and kitchens), per m3 of gas produced
notes: Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): value is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. Wellhead mean 625 Bq/m3 (UNSCEAR 2016 Annex B, n=879; US Johnson 1973 mean 1,370; low 150 is below the UK/Netherlands delivered values) times delivered fraction 0.48 (UNSCEAR delivered 300 over 625); Gesell 1975 gives 0.34 (0.04-0.90) and Mitchell 2016 reports 20-70% decay in pipelines (S0318). Delivered central 300 Bq/m3 reproduces UNSCEAR (0.286 m3/kWh x 300 = 0.75 TBq/GWa for gas power). Independent combination in log-quadrature. Booked only for the Rn that leaves the system; Rn that decays inside pipes and plants is NOT counted as Rn222+ (see the Pb-210 deposit row and choice 3). Includes end-use at burners (route air_delivered_gas). gas_production_m3 is taken as marketed gas; flared and vented gas are handled in their own rows.

description: Rn-222 in vented and fugitive gas released at well sites, plants and pipelines, per m3 of gas produced
notes: Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): value is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. Vented plus fugitive share 2% of marketed gas (0.5-5%): the IEA Global Methane Tracker 2026 gives 36 Mt CH4 from gas operations and 81 Mt from oil and gas together in 2025 against about 2.9 Gt of gas produced (1.3-2.9%). Booked at the wellhead concentration (no decay en route). Flat in time (no earlier data; earlier venting was probably higher). Low confidence.

description: Pb-210 formed from Rn-222 that decays inside gas wells, pipelines and processing plants and plates out (films, scale, sludge), per m3 of gas produced
notes: Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): value is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. Pb-210 head activity = (1 - r) x wellhead Rn-222 x (lambda_Pb210/lambda_Rn222 = 4.715e-4) x deposited fraction p_dep, with r = 0.48 (0.15-0.8), wellhead 625 (150-1400) Bq/m3, p_dep 0.8 (0.4-0.95, assumption). The factor lambda ratio converts Rn-222 atoms that decay in the system to the Pb-210 activity at formation. Po-210 is left to the engine (ingrowth from Pb-210); Po-210 films in gas plants are volatile and not separated. Correlation: (1 - r) is anticorrelated with the delivered-Rn row, so correlated bounds should not be combined across the two rows. Fate at retirement (pipework scrap) is not modelled (gap).

description: Rn-222 released with crude oil handled and refined (equilibrium with Ra-226 in crude), per tonne of crude produced
notes: Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): value is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. Ra-226 in crude oil about 1 Bq/kg adopted by UNSCEAR (0.002 TBq/GWa of oil-fired electricity at about 2 Mt crude per GWa); Bell et al. mean 0.7 Bq/kg, range 0.2-13; IAEA SRS 34 range 0.1-40 Bq/kg. description: Fraction of newly formed scale that stays on tubulars and equipment until retirement
notes: Share of the quantity it splits; shares of one region and era sum to 1 at the central values (bounds are independent bands, not a distribution). Assumption (no measurement). Scale is deposited on tubing and in separators and is mostly removed only at workover or retirement; sludge is assumed removed during operation (no retained fraction, gap). The stream books the retained share in the SAME year as the scale forms, tier rows below, because activity persists unchanged except for decay, which the engine applies from the booking year; no decay survival factor is applied. The retirement lag (about 20 years, 10-35) is instead built into the creation-year windows of the fate rows.

description: Vertical well drill cuttings, uranium-238 activity per well drilled (cuttings mass x activity concentration)
notes: Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): value is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. Cuttings per well 100/250/450 t (NY SGEIS 154 yd3 = 295 t for a 7,000 ft vertical hole, S1201; central lowered to 250 t for the shallower US average well, assumption) times PA DEP TENORM concentration p5/mean/p95 0.63/1.47/3.18 pCi/g (x 0.037 = Bq/g; 17-38 vertical samples, Tables 3-5 and 3-6). Independent log-quadrature combination. Pennsylvania cuttings only (Marcellus-region geology); other plays unmeasured.
